title: Add quantization profile comparison eval job (baseline vs quantized) with gating signal output
author: Olivia Grant
description:
Context: Redwood is shipping an opt-in Quantization Profile Library. We need a first-class eval-harness job type that compares a baseline (fp16/bf16) run vs a quantized run (int8/int4 profile) on the same prompt set(s), then produces a machine-readable pass/fail gating signal that can be used by the profile publish workflow.

This PR adds a new job type `quantization_profile_comparison` that:
- Runs the same eval suite twice (baseline + quantized), enforcing identical prompt set, decode params, and tool/JSON mode settings.
- Stores per-metric deltas (absolute + relative), along with run metadata (model, profile_id/profile_version, hardware tags when provided).
- Emits a compact gating result (`PASS`/`FAIL`/`WARN`) with reasons and threshold references.

Why in eval-harness (vs ad-hoc scripts): We need consistent metrics computation, standardized reporting, and a stable contract for downstream automation (profile publish PR checks + rollbacks).

High-level behavior:
- Baseline run: executes with `execution_mode=baseline` and no quant profile.
- Quantized run: executes with `execution_mode=quantized` and a resolved quantization profile reference (e.g., `qpl://llama3.1-70b/instruct/int4@1.2.0`).
- Comparison: computes metric deltas (e.g., exact match, JSON schema validity, tool-call success rate, toxicity/safety classifiers if present).
- Stats: for configured metrics, uses paired bootstrap CI over item-level scores; fails when regression exceeds threshold AND CI excludes 0 improvement.
- Output: writes `comparison_summary.json` and `gating_signal.json` to the run artifact store; also prints a one-line gate summary suitable for CI logs.

Config example:
```yaml
job_type: quantization_profile_comparison
name: qpl-llama3.1-70b-int4-jsonmode
baseline:
  model: llama3.1-70b-instruct
  runtime:
    provider: redwood
    route: /v1/chat/completions
  params:
    temperature: 0.0
quantized:
  model: llama3.1-70b-instruct
  quantization_profile: qpl://llama3.1-70b-instruct/int4@1.2.0
  runtime:
    provider: redwood
    route: /v1/chat/completions
prompt_sets:
  - promptset://qpl/json_mode_smoke@2024-11-01
  - promptset://qpl/tool_calling_core@2024-11-07
thresholds:
  max_regression:
    json_valid_rate: 0.002
    tool_success_rate: 0.003
  min_improvement:
    tokens_per_second: 0.10
```

Notes:
- This PR intentionally does not define Redwood-wide acceptance thresholds; it supports per-job thresholds with references that can be aligned to the acceptance doc later.
- The job can be used locally (writes artifacts to ./runs) and in CI (uploads to configured artifact backend).

Follow-ups:
- Wire this job into the model-registry profile publish workflow (redwood-model-registry PR) and Redwood monorepo PR checks.
- Add additional metric plugins for long-context and structured-output edge cases as prompt set coverage expands.

review_conversation:
Jonas Weber (review, 2024-11-15): Can we ensure baseline + quantized are identical with respect to prompt randomization and sampling? We’ve been burned by accidental temperature drift.

Olivia Grant (author): Yep. I added a shared `ExecutionPlan` that materializes prompts + per-item decode params once; both runs consume the same plan. Also added a test that fails if either side overrides temperature/top_p unless explicitly allowed.

Selene Huang (review, 2024-11-15): For gating, I’d like a way to fail hard on JSON validity/tool success regressions but allow WARN on “soft” metrics (BLEU-ish / similarity). Can the thresholds config express severity?

Olivia Grant: Added `thresholds.severity_overrides` (optional) so metrics can mark FAIL vs WARN. Defaults to FAIL for validity/safety metrics, WARN otherwise. Also included in `gating_signal.json`.

Priyanka Bose (review, 2024-11-16): Please include profile_id + profile_version separately (not only a single string ref). The model registry manifests need those fields for joining.

Olivia Grant: Done. Parser splits `qpl://...@semver` into `profile_id` and `profile_version` (still retains `profile_ref` for display). Output JSON now includes both fields.

Sana Farid (review, 2024-11-17): Can the summary output include an easy table for dashboards? We ingest JSON but want stable field names.

Olivia Grant: Added `comparison_summary.json` with a stable `rows[]` CSV-like structure in addition to the nested per-metric dict. Kept the nested dict for humans.

Jonas Weber (review, 2024-11-18): Bootstrap CI implementation looks fine, but can you document the decision rule? Specifically: do we require both threshold breach AND CI to exclude 0?

Olivia Grant: Documented in job docstring + README section. Decision rule: fail if |delta| > threshold AND (for configured metrics) CI excludes 0. For metrics without CI config, fall back to threshold-only.

Selene Huang (approval, 2024-11-19): LGTM after severity_overrides change and docs. Please make sure the default thresholds are conservative in examples.

Jonas Weber (approval, 2024-11-19): Approved. This is a good base for the QPL publish gate.

Priyanka Bose (approval, 2024-11-19): Approved.
release_notes: Internal: eval-harness now supports `quantization_profile_comparison` jobs, producing `comparison_summary.json` + `gating_signal.json` artifacts for use as quantization profile publish gates.
